subject: Reserved GPU commitment discussion & isolation needs — follow-up
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Chang <elliot@signalix.ai>; Maya Patel <maya.patel@signalix.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved GPU commitment discussion & isolation needs — follow-up

Hi Elliot / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I’ve attached the MoP we reviewed and a sizing workbook with our suggested starting pool.

Summary of Signalix pain points we captured
- Model latency variability during peak inference windows (p90 spikes impacting user-facing features)
- Data isolation requirement for PII-annotated inference (legal requires tenant-level separation)
- Predictable monthly unit economics for forecasting (want to avoid large over-provisioning)

Goals we agreed on
- Dedicated reserved pool (GPU) for core inference traffic to guarantee p95 < 180ms for 2k qps baseline
- Tenant isolation at the pool level with network and storage separation for PHI/PII workloads
- A procurement path with a 6–12 month committed capacity window and burst to hosted when needed

Proposed technical baseline (from today's discussion)
- Initial commit: 12 x A100-equivalent slots (quantized model flow) — sizing workbook attached
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime for reserved pool; p95 latency SLO of 180ms for production workload (seq len ~512)
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to compatible hosted variant for non-PII routes when pool is saturated

Risks / open questions
- Compliance: need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS integration for the reserved pool (Maya to confirm required KMS vendor)
- Procurement cadence: procurement indicated an internal review cycle of ~4 weeks
- Integration: whether you'll want our Private control plane (VPC) or a Dedicated managed VPC — affects lead time

Next steps (owners & timing)
1) Tessa: Share MoP + sizing workbook (attached) and link to the HubSpot deal — today (done).
2) Maya: Confirm KMS vendor and any additional compliance docs needed — by 2027-06-25.
3) Rishi: Draft commercial outline and a high-level reserved capacity quote — by 2027-06-22.
4) Elliot: Confirm procurement timeline and provide required PO/contract routing info — by 2027-06-30.

If that aligns I'll queue the internal SOW template (sales + legal) and loop Ben for ops readiness questions about burst policies and canary rollout.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: signalix_mop_v1.pdf, reserved_pool_sizing_playbook.xlsx
From: Elliot Chang <elliot@signalix.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@signalix.ai>, procure@signalix.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU commitment discussion & isolation needs — follow-up

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear summary. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) KMS: We use HashiCorp Vault with an internal HSM; procurement/security will need a short doc on KMS integration steps and any required endpoints.
2) Sizing: The 12-slot baseline sounds reasonable as a starting runway; we want a guardrail for soft bursting up to 18 during model retraining windows. Can you include burst OOM behavior in the playbook?
3) Compliance docs: We’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short network topology diagram showing tenant isolation before legal signs off.

Procurement note: our PO approvals usually take 3–5 weeks, but procurement asked for a preliminary quote to include in the upcoming budget review (deadline 2027-07-09).

Action from our side: I’ll ask procurement to share the routing and who should be on any vendor-side contract reviews. Maya will confirm the Vault endpoints early next week.

Best,
Elliot
CTO, Signalix

Adding commercial context — thanks Tessa. Quick pricing sketch to help procurement: 

- 12-slot reserved pool (A100-equivalent) — list price $58,000/month; proposed intake discount (annual commit) -> $46,400/month (20% off)
- Soft burst to 18 slots billed at on-demand premium (we recommend a monthly burst cap setting to limit cost surprises)
- One-time onboarding & private control plane setup fee: $28,000 (covers network config, KMS integration, ops playbook)

I’ll prepare a formal quote and initial SOW draft by end of Tuesday (2027-06-22) that includes: pricing table, SLA language (99.95% reserved pool uptime), canary rollout plan, and a compliance artifact checklist.

Ben — can you confirm ops acceptance testing runbook and whether we can commit to the 180ms p95 at 2k qps baseline for the quantized model? If not, note any caveats for the SOW.

Rishi

Quick ops confirmation —

We can commit to a p95 ~180ms for the quantized model at the 2k qps baseline with the following caveats:
- Baseline assumes a steady sequence length profile (avg 350–550); latency may increase for longer sequences or when model context windows are expanded.
- We’ll require a short acceptance test (2-day canary) during onboarding using your representative production trace.
- KMS integration: our standard pattern supports HashiCorp Vault; will need Vault endpoint details and an on-call for any token exchange testing.

Next steps I’ll own: ops acceptance test plan, the runbook for burst policy behavior, and a short note on fallback routing (how we will route non-PII traffic to hosted variants). I’ll attach the runbook draft to the SOW Rishi prepares.

—Ben
